title: Questions where a word has to be read the owner's way
changed: Nineteen sql cases that were counts and sums a POS already reports are replaced by ten where the answer turns on a definition: lift, new customer, regular, summer, net payout, item margin.
The vendor's definitions go into the prompt. Each owner's own words go into a Definitions document beside their policies, searched and cited like any other section.
Every gold query is its own file, headed by the question, so a reader can check it.
Three policy lookups the owner could read off their own page are dropped; two near misses are added, where the nearest section is the wrong one.

The dataset is regenerated with 24 months, named menus, food costs, one price per item per channel, a promotion, loyalty rewards, seasonal items and regulars who stop coming, so these questions have answers in the data.
conclusion: One wrong-but-safe query in ten. Two rules hidden by the retrieval threshold. One citation slip caught by code. The threshold moves to 0.40 next.
